Rashi on Shabbat 93a:1:1.hebrew: עיגול וקורה גדולים הן, ואין אחד יכול להוציאו:
Rashi on Shabbat 93a:1:1.english: A round cake [of figs] and a beam are large, and one [person] cannot carry it out.

Rashi on Shabbat 93a:1:2.english: And if not - That one [person] is capable of carrying it out.

Rashi on Shabbat 93a:2:1.english: A soul sins - [This] implies [one] soul, and not [many] souls.

Rashi on Shabbat 93a:2:2.english: One [comes] to exclude [a case where] this [person] lifts [it] - from the public domain.

Rashi on Shabbat 93a:2:3.hebrew: וזה מניח - ברשות היחיד, דכל כמה דלא כתיב אלא חד מיעוט, מסתברא דהאי הוא דממעט, דהאי קעביד פלגא והאי פלגא, וליכא חד דמסייע בכולהו:
Rashi on Shabbat 93a:2:3.english: And this [person] places [it] - In the private domain; for as long as only one exclusion is written, it is logical that this [case] is the one that is excluded, since this [person] performs half and that [person performs] half, and there is no single [person] who assists in all of them.

Rashi on Shabbat 93a:2:4.hebrew: וחד - יתורא למעוטי אף על פי דעבדי כי הדדי, דהאי עביד כולה והאי עביד כולה. ומיהו, זה יכול וזה יכול הוא דממעיט, דלאו אורחיה למעבדה בתרי:
Rashi on Shabbat 93a:2:4.english: And one - [i.e., one] superfluous [term comes] to exclude [liability] even though they do [it] together, where this one does all of it and that one does all of it. However, it is [a case where] this one is capable and that one is capable that it excludes, because it is not its normal manner to do it with two [people].

Rashi on Shabbat 93a:2:5.hebrew: וחד - יתורא למעוטי תו זה אינו יכול וזה אינו יכול, דאף על גב דאורחייהו למיעבד בתרי, מעטינהו:
Rashi on Shabbat 93a:2:5.english: And one - [an additional] superfluous [term comes] to further exclude [a case where] this [person] is unable and that [person] is unable, for even though it is their normal way to do [it] as two [people], [Scripture] excluded them.

Rashi on Shabbat 93a:3:1.hebrew: יחיד שעשה בהוראת ב"ד - הורו ב"ד שחלב מותר, והלך היחיד ועשה על פיהם, דאנוס הוא. ורבי שמעון לטעמיה, דאמר בהוריות: יחיד שעשה בהוראת ב"ד חייב:
Rashi on Shabbat 93a:3:1.english: An individual who acted upon the ruling of a court - [Where] the court ruled that forbidden fat is permitted, and the individual went and acted at their word, [he is exempt] because he is [considered] acting under circumstances beyond his control. And Rabbi Shimon follows his own reasoning, as he says in [tractate] Horayot: an individual who acted upon the ruling of a court is liable.

Rashi on Shabbat 93a:4:1.hebrew: תרי מיעוטי כתיבי - נפש אחת חד מיעוטא הוא, דאורחיה דקרא לאישתעי הכי:
Rashi on Shabbat 93a:4:1.english: Two exclusionary [terms] are written - "One person" is one exclusionary [term], for it is the way of Scripture to speak thus.

Rashi on Shabbat 93a:5:1.english: The one who is capable - For he performed all of it.

Rashi on Shabbat 93a:5:2.hebrew: אין בו ממש - מי שאינו אלא מסייע בדבר, ואם בא לעשותו לבדו אינו יכול — אין בו ממש, ולא חשיב מידי, ולא מיפטר אידך:
Rashi on Shabbat 93a:5:2.english: Has no substance - One who merely assists in a matter, and if he comes to do it by himself he is unable [to do so] — he has no substance, and is not considered anything, and the other [person] is not exempted.

Rashi on Shabbat 93a:6:1.english: We, too, also learned - That [something] that assists is insubstantial.

Rashi on Shabbat 93a:6:2.english: He was - a zav sitting on a bed.

Rashi on Shabbat 93a:6:4.hebrew: שאינה יכולה לעמוד על ג' - וכיון דזה אינו יכול וזה אינו יכול, כל אחד ואחד כולי מעשה עביד, וגבי מדרס הזב בעינן שינשא רובו עליו, בת"כ:
Rashi on Shabbat 93a:6:4.english: [Because] it cannot stand on three [legs] - Since this one cannot and that one cannot, each and every one performs the entire act; and regarding the midras [treading-impurity] of a zav, we require that most of his [weight] be borne upon it, [as stated] in Torat Kohanim.

Rashi on Shabbat 93a:6:5.hebrew: ור' שמעון מטהר - ר' שמעון לטעמיה, דאמר זה אינו יכול וזה אינו יכול נמי אינו אלא כמסייע, ופטור. (ל"א: דבעי שיעור זיבה לזה ושיעור זיבה לזה, כלומר רובו של זה מכביד על כל אחד ואחד, ואפילו מסייע לא הוי):
Rashi on Shabbat 93a:6:5.english: And Rabbi Shimon deems [them] ritually pure - Rabbi Shimon [follows] his [own] reasoning, for he says [that in a case where] "neither this one is able nor that one is able," [each] is also only like one who assists, and he is exempt. (Another version: for he requires the measure of zivah [impurity] for this [garment] and the measure of zivah for that [garment] — that is to say, [that] the majority of this [zav's weight] presses down upon each and every one — and [otherwise] it is not even [considered] assisting.)

Rashi on Shabbat 93a:6:6.hebrew: מפני שיכולה לעמוד על ג' - הלכך, כל אחד ואחד ה"ל רביעי ואינו אלא מסייע, וסתמא כר' יהודה, דזה יכול וזה יכול קרי מסייע:
Rashi on Shabbat 93a:6:6.english: Because it can stand on three [legs] - Therefore, each and every one is [considered] a fourth [leg], and it is merely assisting; and [this] anonymous [Mishnah] accords with Rabbi Yehudah, who calls [a case where] this one is able and that one is able "assisting."

Rashi on Shabbat 93a:7:1.hebrew: דעקרה ליה לגמרי - עוקרת הרגל מן הארץ, ואפי' מסייע לא הוי:
Rashi on Shabbat 93a:7:1.english: As [the animal] lifted it completely - [It] lifts the foot off the ground, and it is not even assisting.

Rashi on Shabbat 93a:7:2.hebrew: ופרכינן, ואי טעמא משום דעקרה ליה, כיון דזימנין דעקרה האי וזימנין עקרה האי, ובכל <abbr title="שלש">ג'</abbr> איכא לספוקי שמא הכבידה עליהן ולא עקרתן — לטמינהו מספק, כזב המהפך על <abbr title="חמש">ה'</abbr> פונדאות דמטמינן ליה מספק:
Rashi on Shabbat 93a:7:2.english: And we ask: If the reason is because it lifts it, since sometimes it lifts this [leg] and sometimes it lifts that [leg], and regarding all three [legs] there is room for doubt lest it pressed heavily upon them and did not lift them — let us declare them impure out of doubt, like a zav who turns over on five money belts, which we declare impure out of doubt.

Rashi on Shabbat 93a:7:3.hebrew: פונדאות - כמין חריטין, כיסים ארוכים, ונותנין בהן מעות, ובלעז בריד"ש. וראויין לשמש שכיבה עם מלאכתן, שיושב עליהם והם מלאות מעות ופותח פיהם ונוטל, ואין צריך לומר לו: "עמוד ונעשה מלאכתנו":
Rashi on Shabbat 93a:7:3.english: Money belts - A kind of pouches, long pockets into which one puts coins, and in Old French, brides. And they are fit to serve for lying [upon] along with their [ordinary] use, for one sits upon them while they are full of coins and opens their mouths and takes [coins], and there is no need to say to him, "Stand up and let us do our work."

Rashi on Shabbat 93a:7:4.hebrew: לאורכן - כגון שהיה שוכב על מיעיו או פרקדן, ואורכו מוטל על אורכן:
Rashi on Shabbat 93a:7:4.english: Along their length - For example, [when] he was lying on his stomach or on his back, and his length is laid along their length.

Rashi on Shabbat 93a:7:5.hebrew: טמאים - גרסינן במשנה דטהרות, דיש לומר בכל אחת מהן שנישא רובו עליו, פעמים על זו ופעמים על זו:
Rashi on Shabbat 93a:7:5.english: They are impure - This is the reading in the Mishnah of [the Order of] Tohorot, for one can say regarding each one of them that most of his [weight] was borne upon it, sometimes on this one and sometimes on that one.

Rashi on Shabbat 93a:7:6.hebrew: לרחבן טהורין - לפי שארכו מוטל על רחבן, ואין רובו נישא על אחת מהן:
Rashi on Shabbat 93a:7:6.english: Across their width, they are pure - Because his length lies across their width, and most of him is not borne by any one of them.

Rashi on Shabbat 93a:7:7.english: He slept - [meaning, he slept] on them across their width.

Rashi on Shabbat 93a:7:8.english: [There is] uncertainty [whether] he turned over - along its length, and all of him is found leaning on one of them.

Rashi on Shabbat 93a:7:9.hebrew: טמאות - דכל חדא איכא למימר על זו נתהפך, אלמא מטמינן מספק. והתם נמי, אי משום עקירה הוא, ניטמינהו מספיקא! אלא לאו טעמא משום דכולהו הוו כל חדא וחדא מסייע, ואין בו ממש. כן נראה בעיני משנה זו. ורבותי גורסין: לאורכן טהורין, ופירשו טעמא דלאורכן טהורין משום דאמרי שמא ביניהן שכב ולא עליהם. וקשיא לי: א"כ לקולא תלינן, ואמאי תני סיפא ספק נתהפך טמאים:
Rashi on Shabbat 93a:7:9.english: They are impure - For [regarding] each one, one can say, "He turned over onto this one"; thus we render [objects] impure out of doubt. And there too, if it is because of lifting, let us render them impure out of doubt! Rather, is it not that the reason is because all of them — each and every one — are [merely] assisting, and [that which assists] has no substance? Thus this Mishnah appears to me. But my teachers have the reading, "Along their length — they are pure," and they explained the reason that along their length they are pure is because we say, "Perhaps he lay between them and not upon them." And this is difficult for me: if so, we attribute [uncertainty] leniently, so why does the latter clause teach, "[If] there is uncertainty [whether] he turned over, they are impure"?

Tosafot on Shabbat 93a:2:1.hebrew: תלתא מיעוטי כתיבי - והא דנקט "בעשותה" בברייתא טפי מהנך, משום שהוא מיעוט אחרון שבפסוק, ובהא פליגי. ולא ידע ר"י דאמאי נקט דמילתיה דר' שמעון: "יחיד שעשאה חייב כו'", ולא נקט לישנא דלעיל: "העושה את כולה ולא העושה את מקצתה". ושמא לישנא ד"שנים שעשאוה פטורין" משמע טפי אפי' זה אינו יכול וזה אינו יכול:
Tosafot on Shabbat 93a:2:1.english: Three exclusionary [statements] are written - And [the reason] that [the Tanna] cites "by performing it" in the baraita rather than those other [exclusions is] because it is the last exclusion in the verse, and it is over this [one] that they disagree. And R. Yitzchak does not know why, in the statement of R. Shimon, it cites "an individual who performs it is liable, etc.," and does not cite the phrasing [used] above: "one who performs the whole of it, and not one who performs part of it." Perhaps the phrasing "two who perform it are exempt" implies more [clearly] even [a case where] this [person] is incapable and that [person] is incapable.

Tosafot on Shabbat 93a:2:2.hebrew: חד למעוטי זה עוקר וזה מניח - וזה כתב אות אחת ובא חבירו וכתב אות שניה — לא איצטריך קרא אלא אהוצאה, דה"א אהכנסה ואהוצא' הוא דקפיד רחמנא, וליחייב אפי' בלא הנחה. ה"ג: "ורבי שמעון, יחיד שעשאה בהוראת ב"ד לא צריך קרא", ול"ג "ר"ש לטעמיה, דאמר יחיד שעשאה בהוראת ב"ד חייב" כדפירש בקונטרס; דהא תנן בהדיא בפ"ק דהוריות (ד' ג.): "הלך ועשה על פיהן, בין הביאו כפרתן בין לא כו', ר' שמעון פוטר", ומפרש טעמא: תולה בב"ד אנוס הוא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 93a:2:2.english: One [comes] to exclude [a case where] this one lifts and that one places - And [for the case of] "this one wrote one letter and his fellow came and wrote a second letter," no verse is needed [to exclude it]; rather, [the verse is needed] only for carrying out, for one might have thought that the Merciful One was particular [only] about bringing in and carrying out, so one should be liable even without placing. This is the [correct] reading: "And Rabbi Shimon — an individual who did it by the ruling of the court does not need a verse [to exempt him]," and we do not read: "Rabbi Shimon follows his own reasoning, for he said an individual who did it by the ruling of the court is liable," as Rashi explained; for we explicitly learned in a Mishnah in the first chapter of Horayot (3a): "[If] he went and acted according to their ruling, whether they brought their atonement or not, etc., Rabbi Shimon exempts [him]," and [the Gemara] explains the reason: one who relies on the court is considered coerced.

Tosafot on Shabbat 93a:5:1.hebrew: אמר מר זה יכול וזה אינו יכול - נראה לר"י דהאי אינו יכול היינו אפי' בעל כח הרבה, אלא שהוא נושא הקורה בענין זה בכי האי גוונא שאלמלא אחר לא היה יכול לנושאה לבדו, כגון באצבע או תופשה בענין זה שאינו יכול לנושאה לבדו; דמה לנו לכחו, כיון דהשתא מיהא אינו יכול לנושאה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 93a:5:1.english: The Master said: This [person] is capable and this [person] is incapable - It appears to the Ri that this "incapable" [person] means even one who possesses great strength, except that he is carrying the beam in such a manner—in a case like this—that without the other [person] he would not be able to carry it alone, such as [holding it] with a finger or grasping it in such a manner that he cannot carry it alone; for what does his [general] strength matter to us, since right now, at any rate, he is unable to carry it.

Tosafot on Shabbat 93a:5:2.hebrew: הי מינייהו מיחייב - לא בעי למימר שיהא פטור אותו שיכול וליחייב שאינו יכול, דאין זה סברא; אלא קאמר דליתחייב נמי אפילו שאינו יכול, כמו לר' יהודה ור"מ דאמרי לעיל: "זה אינו יכול וזה אינו יכול — חייב":
Tosafot on Shabbat 93a:5:2.english: Which of them is liable? - [The Gemara] does not mean to say that the one who is capable should be exempt and the one who is incapable should be liable, for that is not logical; rather, it is saying that even the one who is incapable should also be liable, as according to Rabbi Yehudah and Rabbi Meir, who say above: "This one is incapable and this one is incapable — he is liable."

Tosafot on Shabbat 93a:6:1.hebrew: אמר רב זביד משמיה דרבא אף אנן נמי תנינא - פירוש: דמסייע אין בו ממש. קשה לר"י: דהכא אית ליה לרב זביד דמסייע אין בו ממש, וכן רב אשי בסמוך. ובפ"ב דביצה (דף כב.) אמרינן: אמימר כחל עינא על יד נכרי בשבת. א"ל רב אשי: מאי דעתיך כו' ואמר רב כהנא חולה שאין בו סכנה אומר לנכרי ועושה, הא מסייע בהדיה דקא עמיץ ופתח! א"ל: איכא רב זביד דקאי כוותך, ושני ליה: מסייע אין בו ממש. משמע דרב זביד ורב אשי סוברים דיש בו ממש. ואין לומר דהא דאמר הכא "אין בו ממש" — לא שיפטר לגמרי, אלא דאין בו חיוב חטאת; דהא מייתי רב אשי דעבודתו כשרה, משמע דאפי' פסולא דרבנן ליכא. א"כ לענין שבת נמי, מנלן שיש בו איסורא דרבנן? ומיהו לרב אשי איכא למימר דבתר דשמעה מאמימר סברה; אלא לרב זביד קשה, דאיהו גופיה קאמר משמיה דרבא דאין בו ממש, ואמימר היה הרבה אחר רבא, ואפי' אחר רב פפא שהיה תלמידו של רבא. ושמא בתר מעשה דאמימר שמעה רב זביד משמיה דרבא, ולא מרבא עצמו. ועוד אור"י, דהכי פריך התם: והא קא מסייע בהדיה דקא עמיץ ופתח, ואע"ג דמסייע אין בו ממש בעלמא, הא אית לן למימר דאסרו משום שחיקת סממנין; ומשני דאין בו ממש אפילו לענין זה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 93a:6:1.english: Rav Zevid said in the name of Rava: We, too, also learned - Meaning: that one who assists is insubstantial. It is difficult for R"I: for here Rav Zevid holds that one who assists is insubstantial, and likewise Rav Ashi [holds so] immediately below. Yet in the second chapter of Beitzah (22a), we say: Ameimar applied kohl to his eye through a non-Jew on Shabbat. Rav Ashi said to him: "What is your reasoning? etc. [Because] Rav Kahana said: For an ill person who is not in danger, one may tell a non-Jew and he does it — behold, he assists with him, for he closes and opens [his eye]!" He [Ameimar] said to him: "There is Rav Zevid who stands with you [in raising this objection], and I answered him: One who assists is insubstantial." This implies that Rav Zevid and Rav Ashi hold that he [one who assists] has substance. And one cannot say that what it says here, "is insubstantial," means not that he is completely exempt, but rather that there is no obligation of a sin-offering; for Rav Ashi brings [a proof] that his [Temple] service is valid, which implies that there is not even a rabbinic disqualification. If so, with respect to Shabbat as well, from where do we know that there is a rabbinic prohibition in it? However, according to Rav Ashi, one can say that after he heard it from Ameimar, he adopted that view; but according to Rav Zevid it is difficult, for he himself says in the name of Rava that it is insubstantial, whereas Ameimar was much later than Rava, and even after Rav Pappa who was Rava's student. Perhaps after the incident with Ameimar, Rav Zevid heard it in the name of Rava, and not from Rava himself. And furthermore, R"I says that this is what he asks there: "Behold, he assists with him, for he closes and opens [his eye]," and even though one who assists is insubstantial in general, we ought to say that they prohibited it because of grinding medicaments; and he answers that it is insubstantial even with respect to this matter:

Tosafot on Shabbat 93a:6:2.hebrew: ור"ש מטהר - פי' בקונטרס דר"ש לטעמיה, דפטר "זה אינו יכול וזה אינו יכול". [ואינו] נראה לרשב"א, דשאני התם דגלי רחמנא, דאיכא קרא לפטור. ונראה דטעמא משום דבעי שיהיה רוב הזב נישא על כל אחד. וכן משמע במסכת זבים פ"ד (משנה ה), דתנן: הזב בכף מאזנים ומשכב ומושב כנגדו — כרע הזב, טהורין; כרעו הן, טמאין. ר"ש אומר: ביחיד — טמאין, פי' כשאין אלא משכב אחד או מושב אחד; במרובין — טהורין, שאין כ"א נושא רובו:
Tosafot on Shabbat 93a:6:2.english: And Rabbi Shimon deems [them] ritually pure - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained that Rabbi Shimon follows his own reasoning, as he exempts [a case of] "this one cannot [do it alone] and that one cannot [do it alone]." And [this does not] appear [correct] to the Rashba, for there it is different, since the Merciful One revealed [it], as there is a verse to exempt [in that case]. Rather, it appears [to him] that the reason is because we require that the majority of [the weight of] the zav be borne upon each one [of the garments]. And so it is implied in Tractate Zavim, chapter 4 (Mishnah 5), where we learned: "[If] the zav is in one pan of a balance scale, and [items of] mishkav and moshav are opposite him — [if] the zav weighed down [his side], they are ritually pure; [if] they weighed down [their side], they are ritually impure. Rabbi Shimon says: With a single one, they are ritually impure" — meaning, when there is only one mishkav or one moshav; "with multiple [items], they are ritually pure," because each one does not bear his majority.

Tosafot on Shabbat 93a:6:3.hebrew: היה רוכב ע"ג בהמה - בעומדת איירי, דאי במהלכת — כל שעה עוקרת רגל הא' ועומדת על ג', וטמא מה שתחתיהן, שאינה יכולה לעמוד על שתים:
Tosafot on Shabbat 93a:6:3.english: He was riding on an animal - [The Mishnah] is speaking of [an animal] that is standing still, for if [it were] walking, it constantly lifts one leg and stands on three, and what is beneath them would be ritually impure, since it is incapable of standing on two.

Tosafot on Shabbat 93a:6:4.hebrew: מפני שיכולה לעמוד על ג' - וה"ל כל רגל אינו יכול, והג' אחרים יכולין:
Tosafot on Shabbat 93a:6:4.english: "Because it is capable of standing on three [legs]" - And it is [a case of] each leg being incapable [on its own], while the three others are capable:

Tosafot on Shabbat 93a:7:1.hebrew: וכיון דזימנין עקרה הא וזימנין הא ליהוי כזב המתהפך - ואפילו ברה"ר טמא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 93a:7:1.english: And since it sometimes lifts this [foot] and sometimes [lifts] that [foot], it should be like a zav who turns over - And even in a public domain, it is ritually impure.

Tosafot on Shabbat 93a:7:2.hebrew: לאורכן טמאין - כן גריס הקונטרס, ופי' דטמאין משום דאיכא למימר דכל אחד נושא רובו עליו, פעמים על זה ופעמים על זה; לרוחבן טהורין — שאין רובו נישא על כל אחד מהן. ולפי זה אתיא כר"ש, דבעי שיהא רוב הזב נישא עליו. ור"י אומר דמצי למימר דאתיא אפילו כרבנן, וטעמא דטהורות משום דה"ל כל אחד מסייע שאין בו ממש. ומהך רישא הוה מצי למיפרך דמטמאין לאורכן מספיקא, אלא ניחא ליה למיפרך מסיפא, דמפרש בה טעמא אמאי טמאין:
Tosafot on Shabbat 93a:7:2.english: Along their length, they are impure - Thus Rashi reads [the text], and he explained that they are impure because one can say that each one bears most of him, sometimes on this one and sometimes on that one; across their width, they are pure — for most of him is not borne upon any one of them. And according to this, [the Mishnah] follows R. Shimon, who requires that most of the zav be borne upon it. And the Ri says that one can say that it follows even the Rabbis, and the reason they are pure is because each one is [like] an assistant that has no substance. And from this first clause [the Gemara] could have objected that they become impure along their length out of uncertainty, but it preferred to object from the latter clause, in which the reason why they are impure is explicitly stated.
